title: Universal property of a saturated monoscheme blowup
statement: Let $M$ be a fine torsion-free monoscheme with a finite affine cover, and let $I\subset\mathcal M_M$ be a coherent monoid ideal nonempty on every connected component, with monoschemes, local morphisms, ideals and saturated blowups as in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Write $\pi:B=\operatorname{Bl}_I(M)^{\rm sat}\to M$ for the saturated blowup. Then $B$ is saturated, the ideal generated by $\pi^{-1}I$ is locally principal, and for every fine saturated torsion-free monoscheme $Y$ with finite affine cover and every local morphism $f:Y\to M$ for which $f^*I$ is locally principal, there is a unique local morphism $\widetilde f:Y\to B$ with $\pi\widetilde f=f$. Here locally principal means that near each point the ideal is generated by one section of the monoid sheaf. If $M=\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$ and $I$ has finite nonempty generating set $E$, then on the open locus where $f(a)$ generates $f^*I$, for $a\in E$, this lift factors through the chart $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}(P[I-a])^{\rm sat}$ and its homomorphism on group completions extends that induced by $f$. The unique lifts commute with restriction to open subsets and with precomposition whenever the precomposed morphism satisfies the same hypotheses.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.19 and 3.1.21, printed p.101, with local blowup charts in 3.1.19. No Stacks tag states this monoscheme universal property.

proof.text: Work on an affine base chart $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$. It has a unique closed point $P\setminus P^\times$: every proper prime ideal is contained in it, and any basic open containing it is the whole spectrum. Thus local finite generation of $I$ at this point gives a finite generating set $E\subset P$ on the whole chart. This set is nonempty. Indeed, an empty ideal on an affine chart stays empty on its restrictions, whereas an ideal generated by a nonempty set stays nonempty at every stalk. Affine monoid spectra are irreducible (the empty prime belongs to every nonempty basic open), hence connected. If charts intersect they consequently have the same empty/nonempty alternative. The unions of charts of the two alternatives are disjoint opens, so nonemptiness on each connected component excludes the empty alternative. For $a\in E$ set $Q_a=\langle P,b-a\ (b\in E)\rangle\subset P^{\rm gp}$ and $C_a=Q_a^{\rm sat}$. The prescribed blowup has charts $B_a=\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}C_a$. The finite-saturation lemma makes $C_a$ fine saturated; it also makes every localization saturated, since for saturated $C_a$ its displayed localization equality reads $(C_a-S)^{\rm sat}=C_a-S$. Thus all stalks of $B$ are saturated. On $B_a$, $b=a+(b-a)$ for every $b\in E$, so the pulled-back ideal is $a+\mathcal M_B$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.3--3.1.4, 3.1.17--3.1.21; fineness, saturation, and chartwise principalization

proof.text: For every open $U\subset Y$, $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal M_Y)$ is integral by stalkwise cancellation. It is saturated in $A^{\rm gp}$: if $g=s-t$ with $ng\in A$, its image at each stalk belongs to the stalk monoid by saturation. Represent this image by a section $r_x$ near $x$. Shrinking enforces $r_x+t=s$. On intersections these sections agree by cancellation, so the sheaf axiom glues a section $r$ with $r+t=s$, which represents $g$ in $A$. This uses integrality and saturation of the actual unsharpened stalks; units need not vanish.

source.place: VIII 3.1.6, 3.1.17; elementary passage from saturated integral stalks to sections

proof.text: Over an affine base chart write $h:P\to\Gamma(f^{-1}\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P,\mathcal M_Y)$ for the pullback of sections. At a point $y$, let $t$ generate $f^*I$ in $\mathcal M_{Y,y}$. Membership of $t$ in the ideal gives $t=h(a)+u$ for some $a\in E$; conversely $h(a)=t+v$. Cancellation gives $u+v=0$, so $u$ is a unit. Consequently $h(a)$ also generates. For each of the finitely many $b\in E$ choose $r_b$ with $h(b)=h(a)+r_b$ at $y$; represent these germs and their equalities on a common neighborhood $U$. Then $h(a)$ generates on $U$. These neighborhoods cover $Y$. In particular the locus $U_a$ on which a fixed $h(a)$ generates is open, being the locus where the finitely many divisibility relations hold locally.

source.place: VIII 3.1.18--3.1.19; finite-generator neighborhoods without assuming sharpness

proof.text: On any open $U$ where $h(a)$ generates, put $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal M_Y)$. Local solutions of $h(b)=h(a)+r_b$ agree by cancellation and glue to sections $r_b\in A$. Extend $h$ to $h^{\rm gp}:P^{\rm gp}\to A^{\rm gp}$ by $p-q\mapsto h(p)-h(q)$. This sends every $b-a$ to $r_b$, hence maps $Q_a$ into $A$. If $c\in C_a$, choose $n>0$ with $nc\in Q_a$; step 2 gives $h^{\rm gp}(c)\in A$. Restriction therefore defines $k_a:C_a\to A$. This extension of $h$ is unique: the inclusions $P\subseteq Q_a\subseteq C_a\subseteq P^{\rm gp}$ identify all group completions with $P^{\rm gp}$, so any extension to the integral monoid $A$ has group map $h^{\rm gp}$. Apply the unsharpened affine Hom bijection to $k_a$, using fineness of $C_a$, to obtain a local map $U\to B_a$. The naturality and injectivity of that bijection identify its composite to the base chart with $f|_U$. This also proves the required group-completion formula.

source.place: VIII Lemma 3.1.8(i), 3.1.17--3.1.21; construction on a principalizing chart

proof.text: In the $e$-chart of $B$, the ideal is $e+\mathcal M_B$. At a point of that chart, $a$ is also a generator exactly when $a-e$ is a unit: if $e=a+v$, then $(a-e)+v=0$ by cancellation, and the converse uses this unit inverse. By the spectrum definition its unit locus is $D(a-e)$, exactly the prescribed overlap with the $a$-chart. Thus $B_a$ is precisely the locus where $a$ generates. Now let $g:U\to B$ be any local lift of $f|_U$, where $h(a)$ generates. Choose an $e$-chart containing $g(y)$. The image of $e$ also generates at $y$, so the image of $a-e$ is a unit. Locality of the stalk map forces $a-e$ to be a unit at $g(y)$. The overlap description puts $g(y)$ in $B_a$. This proves that every such lift factors through $B_a$. Its section map extends $h$, hence equals $k_a$ by step 4. The affine Hom bijection forces equality with the lift already constructed. This proves uniqueness on every principalizing open, including all of $U_a$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.5--3.1.8(i), 3.1.19--3.1.21; generator loci and uniqueness of both point and sheaf maps

proof.text: For a fixed affine base chart, constructed lifts agree on source overlaps by step 5. For two different base charts, cover the intersection of their images by affine opens subordinate to both charts. On a basic base restriction $P-S$, the unsaturated chart is $Q_a-S$, and its saturation is $C_a-S$ by the finite-saturation lemma. Thus the prescribed blowup gluing restricts to the same construction on basic opens; the sheaf gluing definition then gives the assertion on arbitrary open restrictions. Applying steps 3--5 there proves equality on the source overlaps as well. Glue the continuous maps by agreement on the open cover. On an open of $B$, glue their compatible section homomorphisms using the sheaf axiom of $\mathcal M_Y$; these give a sheaf map whose stalk maps are the local maps already constructed. This defines the required local morphism $\widetilde f:Y\to B$. Any other lift agrees on the neighborhoods of step 3 by step 5, hence agrees globally. Thus the lift exists and is unique with all the stated chart properties.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19--3.1.21; open gluing of the explicitly constructed local lifts

proof.text: Restriction of $\widetilde f$ to an open subset is a lift of the restricted morphism. If $g:Z\to Y$ is an admissible precomposition, then $\widetilde f\circ g$ is a local lift of $f\circ g$, since its composite with $\pi$ is $f\circ g$. The uniqueness proved locally in step 5 and globally in step 6 identifies these maps with the prescribed lifts. The proof of uniqueness applies to open subsets without any finite-cover requirement, so restriction causes no extra hypothesis. If $Y$ is empty the continuous map and its sheaf map are unique. The same chartwise construction treats disconnected $M$ and $Y$ component by component.

source.place: VIII 3.1.21--3.1.22; restriction and precomposition from uniqueness

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII 3.1.19--3.1.21, with Lemma 3.1.8(i); explicit chart expansion of the universal-property argument.

The landed node states ILO VIII 3.1.8(i) for fine P and any (T,A): a bijection Hom_loc to A(P) = Hom(P, Gamma), natural in both arguments, with no sharpness assumption. Steps 4-5 use only that bijection, its naturality in P and its injectivity, applied to fine C_a. Sources checked in ILO VIII: 3.1.8(i) on p.99, and 3.1.19 and 3.1.21 on p.101; the statement is a faithful, unweakened reading of 3.1.21. Steps: (1) the closed point P minus units gives a global finite nonempty E; finite saturation makes C_a fine saturated with saturated localizations; b=a+(b-a) makes the ideal principal. (2) Section monoids of Y are integral and saturated, by gluing stalk witnesses with cancellation. (3) Generators differ by units (u+v=0), so the loci U_a are open. (4) k_a: C_a -> A exists by step 2 and is unique because all group completions are P^gp; the Hom bijection and its naturality give the lift. (5) B_a meets B_e in D(a-e); locality forces any lift into B_a; injectivity of the bijection gives uniqueness. (6) Gluing uses (Q_a-S)^sat=C_a-S. (7) Restriction and precomposition follow from uniqueness. Edge cases checked: P=N, P a group, the unit ideal on a non-saturated P, the diagonal N->N^2 with I=(e1,e2), and empty Y. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses; all cited nodes are in sk-i-curve-zero (no tool_uses); no SGA.
